messages:
Sasha: heads up — since the prefix-cache change landed we see more tiny continuous batches and overall token/s down ~12% in canary :eyes:
Mike: any idea if this is batching policy or the KV checks adding enqueue latency?
Sasha: I profiled enqueuer; enqueue latency median +3.6ms, p95 +12ms. looks like we now do a cache-hit probe synchronously which delays batching window.
Lee: hmm that would make the batching window often expire with small batch sizes. did kernel selection also change? small batches pick the high-overhead but low-latency kernel and that hurts throughput.
Ana: quick numbers from perf job: baseline tokens/s=980k, post-change=860k. avg batch size dropped 21% (6.2 -> 4.9).
Jules: that aligns. if cache hits reduce "uncached token" budgets, existing packer estimates are wrong. packer still sorts by total_request_length not by uncached_length.
Sasha: proposal: make packer cache-hit-aware. assign weight = max(1, estimated_uncached_tokens) and pack to hit token_budget_target (e.g. 512 uncached tokens) instead of total tokens.
Mike: sounds reasonable. can we estimate uncached_tokens cheaply? we have prefix_len in kv metadata. if prefix fully cached: uncached_tokens = requested_new_tokens. partial cache: uncached = total_len - cached_prefix_len.
Lee: need to be careful: computing cached_prefix_len is currently the expensive probe. compute a fast probe during admission that returns cached_prefix_len_estimate via bloom or cache-metadata header to avoid reading KV inline. ops-bot can expose a fast-miss hint.
ops-bot: suggestion: add lightweight cache-index check that returns prefix_hit_length in <0.5ms.
Jules: alternative: optimistic packing: assume full-cache hit for large prefixes, then if miss adjust in-flight scheduling? painful. better to have estimate.
Ana: also watch kernel selection fallback: small batches tend to trigger kernel_x_small which has high per-batch overhead. we should route based on uncached_tokens too: if uncached_tokens>128 use kernel_large_batch path even if batch_size small.
Sasha: adding pseudocode for packing policy we want to try in A/B:
```
# admission path (simplified)
prefix_hit = fast_index_lookup(request.prefix_id)  # <0.5ms hint
uncached = request.total_tokens - prefix_hit.length
request.weight = max(1, uncached)
# packer: fill until sum(weight) >= UNCACHED_TOKEN_TARGET (512) or wall_clock_deadline
```
Mike: nice. we should also change the queue policy: currently FIFO with size cap. switch to weighted queue where peek uses weight to decide which requests to include in next batch.
Lee: I'll implement weighted-peek packer. two caveats: 1) fairness (don't starve tiny uncached requests), 2) preemption across tenants. add per-tenant max-weight in admission.
Jules: test plan: run 24h canary with 50/50 traffic, measure tokens/s, avg latency P50/P95, batch size distribution, and kernel selection counters. also record cache-hit distribution.
Ana: baseline metrics to compare: tokens/s, avg_batch_size, median_enqueue_latency, p95_enqueue_latency, kernel_switch_count.
Sasha: quick simulated numbers from local simulation (synthetic mix): old packing: tokens/s 970k, avg_batch 6.1; naive change (synchronous kv probe) tokens/s 845k, avg_batch 4.8; new weight-based packer with fast-index hint tokens/s 1015k, avg_batch 6.5.
Mike: great if sim holds. risk: fast-index adds memory and needs to be available on private deployments. fallback: if no fast-index, use conservative estimate (assume no cache) to preserve throughput at cost of slightly higher compute.
Lee: also add kernel-selection tweak: if sum(uncached_tokens) >= 256 pick kernel_A (throughput-optimized) even if batch_size<4. that avoids per-batch kernel overhead.
Jules: let's also capture CI perf regression trigger: if tokens/s drops >5% or avg_batch_size drops >10% post-deploy, auto-roll and alert #eng-sre.
Sasha: next steps: Lee will branch packer, Mike will add fast-index RPC hook, Ana will add perf job, Jules will wire canary checks. Aim for canary by EOD+2. :rocket:

Sasha: thanks all. keeping thread here for updates and quick logs. +1 to running the A/B and kernel tweaks before sweeping to Private customers.
